messages:
Sam: FYI saw a spike of SAST/DAST failures after the dep bump merge batch (approx 18 PRs). Failing job shows KMS decrypt denies for the scanner SA.
scan-bot: alert: multi-pr-scan-failure detected for repo: infra-services. Grouped 18 failures across pipelines. See CI job: https://ci.redwood/internal/6789
Lina: Do we have a single root cause or multiple? Can someone paste the deny log?
Omar: Pasted from one job: ```
2026-03-23T02:05:11Z ERROR: PermissionDenied: kms.cryptoKeys.decrypt denied for serviceAccount:scanner@redwood.iam.
requestId: abcd-1234
```
Priya: That maps to a missing binding on the active KMS key version. AuditLog shows a role removal event at 2026-03-22T23:59 by infra-maintainer@redwood.iam (change-id: CHG-20260322-77).
Sam: Ugh, noisy for app owners. Idea: centralize triage for dependency-bump waves and provide a single ticket with all affected PRs.
Lina: +1. Also, we should avoid flipping SAST to hard-block during large batched upgrades. Maybe mark as "scan-warning" for first 10 PRs in a rolling 24h window.
Omar: Short-term remediation: re-add minimal binding. Example (GCP):
```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/p/locations/global/keyRings/r/cryptoKeys/k 
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner@redwood.iam 
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
Sam: Can infra restore that and record the exact change (who/when) in the change ticket? Compliance needs the audit too.
Priya: I can export the KMS admin audit entries to the compliance BigQuery dataset. Retention 395 days as per policy. I'll include keyVersion and requestMetadata.
scan-bot: created ticket SEC-2026-224, attached grouped CI logs and initial audit entries.
Lina: Longer-term: we should implement ephemeral CI grants for scanner SA. Flow: CI job requests short-lived decrypt grant via KMS-GrantService -> audit entry + TTL enforcement. That removes standing permissions.
Omar: Architecturally fine but requires a vault/KMS bridge and authorizer; estimate ~2w dev + infra testing. We should backlog it as P2 security project.
Sam: Also, automation request: create a webhook that, upon scan failures, will: 1) correlate failures to shared cause (same KMS principal or rule), 2) create a single triage issue with all PRs, 3) tag owner from CODEOWNERS or fallback to security oncall. Lina can you draft the webhook spec?
Lina: I will draft. For matching rules use: (a) identical KMS principal, (b) identical failing rule hash, (c) overlapping dependency file path.
Priya: Add to the runbook a step to snapshot the KMS deny audit payload and GCP IAM bindings before making changes. We need that for any post-incident compliance review.
Omar: Also propose adding a temporary heuristic to the scanner: if X failures in Y minutes for the same dependency family, mark as non-blocking with a comment that links to the triage issue. This prevents CI churn for app teams.
Sam: Agree. Assignments: Lina -> webhook spec + initial runbook edit; Omar -> short-term remediation command + implement scanner heuristic prototype; Priya -> BigQuery export & audit snapshot; Sam -> create infra change request to restore binding and reference SEC-2026-224.
scan-bot: noted assignments and reminded oncall. If anyone changes IAM bindings, please include CHG-id and link to SEC-2026-224. :white_check_mark:
Lina: One more thing: adjust PR templates to include a `scan-owner:` label that CI/webhook can set automatically. Helps routing.
Sam: Great call. Let's keep this thread as the source of truth until the ticket is closed. If the restore doesn't fix >2 jobs, escalate to oncall.@oncall
Priya: I'll attach the exact audit rows to the ticket and set the BigQuery job to start export immediately.
Omar: I'll open a github issue for the scanner heuristic and PR a prototype.
Lina: Draft incoming in ~2h. Thanks everyone.
